pr.title: Cap refunds at the captured amount
pr.author: sample-author
pr.head: 4f1c9e07b2d84a6f9c3e1d2b7a5f0e8c6d9b3a21

verdict.label: Merge after one answer
verdict.summary: Refunds are now capped at what was captured, counting earlier partial refunds, and the check runs inside a row lock so two parallel refunds can't both pass. Tests prove both. One open question: whether anything else writes refunds without going through this service.

asked: Sum of refunds never exceeds the captured amount: done (step 1)
Two refunds at the same moment can't both succeed: done (step 1)
extra: Gateway calls now send an idempotency key (step 1)

steps.title: Refund total is checked inside a row lock
steps.say: Boss fight! This is where the money moves. Two of my mutants got caught, but one escaped...
steps.why: Before, each refund was compared only with the captured amount, so three refunds of 60 on a 100 payment all passed. Now the service sums earlier refunds (skipping failed ones) and checks the total. The payment row is locked `FOR UPDATE` for the whole transaction, so a second refund waits instead of reading a stale sum.
look: The sum skips `failed` refunds. Pending ones count, which is the safe side.
The gateway call happens inside the transaction. If it is slow, the row lock is held that long.
`idempotencyKey: refund.id` means a retried request can't refund twice at the gateway.

evidence.text: `refund.service.spec.ts`: 9 tests pass on head, including the new partial and parallel cases.
Removed `lock: 'FOR UPDATE'`: "lets only one of two parallel refunds through" went red.
Dropped `alreadyRefunded` from the check: "rejects a partial refund that would pass the captured total" went red.
Removed the `idempotencyKey`: every test still passes. Nothing checks it.
`RefundController` and the `refund.requested` queue worker both call `RefundService.refund`. No other code inserts into `refunds`.

questions: Does the support dashboard or a script write refunds straight to the database? Those would skip this check.

hunks.note: The lock, the sum, and the check all happen in one transaction.

steps.title: Partial index for the refund sum
steps.say: Just an index. But I only have the author's word that it ran fine. Hmm...
steps.why: Every refund now sums the earlier refunds for its payment. The index keeps that a lookup, and `CONCURRENTLY` builds it without locking the table.
look: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` can't run inside a transaction. Check that the migration runner allows that.

evidence.text: The PR body says the migration ran on a staging copy in 4 s.

steps.title: Three new refund tests
steps.say: These tests are the receipts! I broke the fix on purpose and they caught it.
steps.why: These are the PR's proof: a partial refund past the total, two parallel refunds, and failed refunds left out of the sum.
look: The parallel test runs against a real Postgres in CI, so the lock is real.

evidence.text: All three pass on head, and two of them are the ones that caught the step 1 mutants.

steps.title: Error class and code renamed
steps.say: A rename. Safe to skip, unless some client still matches the old code.
steps.why: `RefundTooLargeError` becomes `RefundExceedsCaptureError` and carries the captured and refunded totals.
look: API clients that match on `refund_too_large` will stop matching.

evidence.text: No other code in the repo uses the old name or code.

questions.text: Does anything write to `refunds` without going through `RefundService`? A direct insert skips the cap.
Do any clients match on the old `refund_too_large` code?

gaps: No test fails if the gateway idempotency key is removed.
method: Sample data for the README. In a real run, tests and mutations run on the PR head in a separate worktree, and code excerpts are cut from the PR diff by `build.py`.
